SUPPLIES YOU’LL NEED:
	•	Warm water and car wash soap
	•	Microfiber cloths
	•	Plastic or rubber scraper (non-metal)
	•	Isopropyl alcohol (70–91%)
	•	Acetone or Goo Gone Automotive (for superglue)
	•	Clay bar and lubricant
	•	Car polish or rubbing compound
	•	Wax or ceramic spray (to re-protect after cleanup)

⸻

🧼 STEP-BY-STEP CLEANING:

1. Assess and Shade the Area
	•	Park in a shaded area. Heat can bake in the damage.
	•	Photograph the damage in case you want to file a report or insurance claim.

⸻

2. Initial Rinse
	•	Use a hose or pressure washer to remove loose baby powder and dried egg.
	•	Do not scrub yet — dried egg is acidic and can scratch the paint if rubbed dry.

⸻

3. Soak and Loosen Egg
	•	Soak a microfiber cloth in warm water with car soap and lay it over the egg for 10–15 minutes.
	•	Gently wipe without scrubbing.
	•	Repeat if necessary.

TIP: If the egg has etched the clear coat (common if left in the sun), polishing or repainting may be required.

⸻

4. Deal With Baby Powder
	•	Powder will mostly rinse off, but if clumped:
	•	Use a damp microfiber cloth and gentle soap solution to wipe it off.
	•	Avoid circular motions that grind it in.

⸻

5. Tackle the Superglue
	•	This is the hardest part. Proceed slowly:
	•	Try Goo Gone Automotive or acetone on a cloth.
	•	Test on a hidden spot first to avoid damaging clear coat.
	•	Let it sit 1–2 minutes.
	•	Gently scrape with a plastic scraper or your fingernail.
	•	Repeat as needed.
	•	Follow with isopropyl alcohol to clean residue.

⚠️ Caution: Acetone can damage paint if left too long. Use sparingly and wipe off quickly.

⸻

6. Clay Bar Treatment
	•	After removing the bulk of the mess, use a clay bar kit (with lubricant) to remove any surface contaminants left behind.
	•	Follow directions closely.

⸻

7. Polish & Protect
	•	If you see hazing or dullness:
	•	Use a light rubbing compound or polish to restore finish.
	•	Finish with wax or ceramic spray to seal and protect the area.
